reasons: No visual test appears in the packet.
Some rules rely on calc values that could be invalid at narrow widths.

terms.meaning: the stylesheet language that controls how the interface looks
a rule that applies only when the screen is a certain width or the user has a certain preference
a unit of size based on the base font size of the page
a number that controls which element is drawn on top of another
a named value, here the timeline space, that many rules can read

depends_on: workspace layout classes from the viewer interface

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Stylesheet introduction
sections.what: A comment stating that the 3D view fills the screen and the tools float above it.
sections.why: Sets the intent for the rules that follow.

sections.name: .viewer-shell.workspace
sections.title: Base workspace layout
sections.what: Sets the workspace to be the positioning reference and creates a header row and a main row.
sections.why: Makes the 3D view the base that everything else is placed on.
sections.watch_out: Other rules use this as their positioning reference, so changing it moves all overlays.

sections.name: .viewer-shell.workspace.has-timeline
sections.title: Space for timeline
sections.what: Sets the reserved bottom space to a fixed amount when the timeline is shown.
sections.why: Keeps the 3D view and tools from sitting under the timeline.
sections.watch_out: The value must match the actual timeline height or content will be hidden.

sections.name: .viewer-shell.workspace.has-lifecycle
sections.title: Space for lifecycle strip
sections.what: Sets a larger reserved bottom space when the lifecycle strip is shown.
sections.why: The lifecycle strip is taller than the timeline, so it needs more room.
sections.watch_out: Keep this value in step with the lifecycle strip height.

sections.name: .viewer-shell.workspace .viewer-header
sections.title: Header padding in workspace
sections.what: Reduces the header padding inside the workspace.
sections.why: Keeps the header compact so the 3D view gets more room.

sections.name: @media (max-width: 1100px)
sections.title: Header row on narrow screens
sections.what: Lets the header grow to fit wrapped tabs on screens up to 1100px wide.
sections.why: Stops the header from being cut off when its tabs wrap to a second row.
sections.watch_out: The fixed header height on wide screens would clip wrapped tabs if this rule were removed.

sections.name: .viewer-shell.workspace .viewer-body
sections.title: Viewer body fills area
sections.what: Makes the viewer body block-shaped and hides any overflow.
sections.why: Prevents scrollbars from appearing around the 3D view.

sections.name: .viewer-shell.workspace .stage
sections.title: 3D stage fills viewer
sections.what: Places the 3D stage absolutely so it covers the whole viewer.
sections.why: The 3D view should sit behind all floating tools.

sections.name: .viewer-shell.workspace .stage-badge
sections.title: Stage name badge placement
sections.what: Positions the badge in the top left corner, keeps it on one line and hides overflow.
sections.why: Shows the current view name without blocking the dock.
sections.watch_out: The maximum width uses a subtraction that may become invalid on small screens.

sections.name: .viewer-shell.workspace .stage-badge small
sections.title: Hide small badge text
sections.what: Hides small text inside the stage badge.
sections.why: Keeps the badge compact.

sections.name: .viewer-shell.workspace .stage-hint
sections.title: Stage hint placement
sections.what: Places a hint in the top right corner, with a truncated single line.
sections.why: Gives a short tip without taking space from the dock.
sections.watch_out: Same width subtraction concern as the badge.

sections.name: .viewer-shell.workspace .overlay-panel
sections.title: Overlay spacing
sections.what: Adds top padding and bottom padding that depends on the timeline space.
sections.why: Keeps overlay content clear of the dock and timeline.

sections.name: .viewer-shell.workspace .cinematic-subtitle
sections.title: Cinematic subtitle placement
sections.what: Centres the subtitle near the bottom with a limited width and height, scrolling if needed.
sections.why: Keeps subtitles readable above the timeline.

sections.name: .viewer-shell.workspace > .timeline-panel
sections.title: Timeline panel placement
sections.what: Places the timeline at the bottom centre with a frosted background and border.
sections.why: Gives the timeline a consistent place above the 3D view.
sections.watch_out: Its z-index must stay below the floating panels and above the stage.

sections.name: .timeline-panel[hidden]
sections.title: Hidden timeline stays hidden
sections.what: Forces the timeline to disappear when its hidden attribute is set.
sections.why: The default display rule would otherwise override the hidden state.

sections.name: .workspace-dock
sections.title: Dock bar layout
sections.what: Places the dock bar at the top centre as a rounded, scrollable row.
sections.why: Gives all panel toggles a single place.

sections.name: .workspace-dock button
sections.title: Dock button look
sections.what: Styles each dock button as a small rounded label with muted text.
sections.why: Keeps buttons compact and readable.

sections.name: .workspace-dock button[aria-pressed="true"]
sections.title: Pressed dock button
sections.what: Shows a pressed dock button with light background and dark text.
sections.why: Lets the user see which panels are open.
sections.watch_out: The pressed state depends on the aria-pressed attribute set in the dock component.

sections.name: .workspace-dock button:hover
sections.title: Dock button hover
sections.what: Brightens the text of an unpressed dock button on hover.
sections.why: Shows the button is clickable.

sections.name: .workspace-dock button[aria-pressed="true"]:hover
sections.title: Pressed dock button hover
sections.what: Keeps the dark text on a pressed dock button when hovered.
sections.why: Stops the hover colour from hiding a pressed button's label.

sections.name: .workspace-dock .dock-clear
sections.title: Clear view button style
sections.what: Adds a divider line and gold text to the last dock button.
sections.why: Makes the clear or show button stand apart from the panel toggles.

sections.name: .floating-panel
sections.title: Floating panel base
sections.what: Gives each floating tool a border, rounded corners, shadow, blur and a column layout.
sections.why: Makes tools look like separate floating windows above the 3D view.
sections.watch_out: Z-index must stay above the stage.

sections.name: .floating-panel:hover
sections.title: Floating panel on hover
sections.what: Raises a floating panel slightly when the mouse is over it.
sections.why: Keeps the panel the user is working with on top.

sections.name: .floating-panel-header
sections.title: Floating panel header
sections.what: Styles the drag handle at the top of a panel with a grab cursor and a divider.
sections.why: Shows where the user can drag the panel.
sections.watch_out: Touch dragging depends on the touch action setting here.

sections.name: .floating-panel.collapsed .floating-panel-header
sections.title: Collapsed panel header
sections.what: Removes the divider line when a panel is collapsed.
sections.why: Keeps a collapsed panel neat.

sections.name: .floating-panel-header:active
sections.title: Header while dragging
sections.what: Changes the cursor to a closed hand while the header is pressed.
sections.why: Shows the panel is being moved.

sections.name: .floating-panel-header strong
sections.title: Panel title text
sections.what: Styles the panel title as small uppercase monospaced text.
sections.why: Gives a consistent label style for each panel.

sections.name: .floating-grip
sections.title: Drag grip symbol
sections.what: Styles the small grip marks at the header with dim colour and tight spacing.
sections.why: Hints that the header can be dragged.

sections.name: .floating-panel-header button
sections.title: Header buttons
sections.what: Makes header buttons small, square and transparent with a pointer cursor.
sections.why: Gives collapse and close controls a compact look.

sections.name: .floating-panel-header button:hover
sections.title: Header button hover
sections.what: Highlights a header button's background and text on hover.
sections.why: Shows the button responds to the mouse.

sections.name: .floating-panel-body
sections.title: Panel body scrolling
sections.what: Lets the panel body fill space and scroll when its content is long.
sections.why: Keeps long tools usable inside a fixed-size panel.

sections.name: .floating-panel .inspector
sections.title: Inspector inside a panel
sections.what: Removes the inspector's own border, scrolling and background so it blends into the panel.
sections.why: Avoids double borders and nested scrollbars.

sections.name: @media (max-width: 760px)
sections.title: Panels on small screens
sections.what: Makes floating panels nearly full width on screens up to 760px, overriding their set width.
sections.why: Keeps tools usable on phones.
sections.watch_out: The important flag overrides any width set elsewhere, so it is hard to change later.

sections.name: .element-layers
sections.title: Element list spacing
sections.what: Adds padding around the element layers list.
sections.why: Keeps the list readable.

sections.name: .element-layers ul
sections.title: Element list layout
sections.what: Removes list bullets and spaces the rows in a grid.
sections.why: Shows the layers as a tidy list.

sections.name: .element-layers li.layer-schedule-only
sections.title: Schedule-only layer row
sections.what: Lays out a layer row in four columns with a pointer cursor.
sections.why: Gives each layer row a swatch, name and value area.

sections.name: .element-layers li.layer-schedule-only
sections.title: Schedule-only layer row, no action
sections.what: Changes the schedule-only layer row to three columns with a default cursor and muted text.
sections.why: Shows rows that cannot be clicked as informational.
sections.watch_out: Both schedule-only rules target the same selector, so the later one wins for the layout.

sections.name: .element-layers li label:hover
sections.title: Layer row hover
sections.what: Adds a background to a layer row on hover.
sections.why: Shows the row is interactive.

sections.name: .element-layers i
sections.title: Layer colour swatch
sections.what: Gives the colour swatch a fixed size and rounded corners.
sections.why: Keeps swatches the same size in every row.

sections.name: .layer-swatch-outline
sections.title: Outline swatch
sections.what: Draws a dashed outline swatch for layers without a fill colour.
sections.why: Distinguishes unfilled layers.

sections.name: .element-layers small
sections.title: Layer count text
sections.what: Styles the small count text in a dim colour with tabular numbers.
sections.why: Keeps numbers aligned in the list.

sections.name: .layer-color-toggle
sections.title: Layer colour toggle
sections.what: Lays out the colour toggle in a row with small text.
sections.why: Puts the colour checkbox beside its label.

sections.name: .checklist-panel .floating-panel-body
sections.title: Checklist panel body
sections.what: Makes the checklist panel body a column that does not scroll itself.
sections.why: Lets the inner checklist scroll instead.

sections.name: .work-checklist
sections.title: Checklist container
sections.what: Makes the checklist a flexible column.
sections.why: Lets the checklist fill the panel.

sections.name: .checklist-progress
sections.title: Checklist progress summary
sections.what: Lays out the progress summary as a padded grid.
sections.why: Shows progress above the checklist.

sections.name: .checklist-progress small
sections.title: Checklist progress note
sections.what: Styles the small note under the progress summary.
sections.why: Adds detail in dim, smaller text.

sections.name: .checklist-meter
sections.title: Progress bar track
sections.what: Draws a thin rounded grey track for the progress bar.
sections.why: Shows how far the work is complete.

sections.name: .checklist-meter span
sections.title: Progress bar fill
sections.what: Draws the green fill inside the progress track and animates its width.
sections.why: Shows completed share visually.

sections.name: .checklist-filters
sections.title: Checklist filters
sections.what: Lays out two filter controls side by side with a divider below.
sections.why: Lets the user filter tasks by two criteria.

sections.name: .checklist-filters input
sections.title: Filter text input
sections.what: Styles the filter input with border, background and small text.
sections.why: Makes the search box match other controls.

sections.name: .checklist-scroll
sections.title: Checklist scroll area
sections.what: Makes the list scroll inside its panel.
sections.why: Keeps long checklists usable.

sections.name: .checklist-group h3
sections.title: Checklist group heading
sections.what: Makes group headings stick to the top of the scroll area with uppercase monospaced text.
sections.why: Keeps the current group name visible while scrolling.
sections.watch_out: The background colour is needed so text below does not show through.

sections.name: .checklist-group h3 small
sections.title: Group heading count
sections.what: Dims the count shown next to a group heading.
sections.why: Keeps the count secondary.

sections.name: .checklist-group ul
sections.title: Checklist group list
sections.what: Removes list bullets and spacing from group lists.
sections.why: Keeps items flush.

sections.name: .checklist-group li button
sections.title: Checklist item button
sections.what: Lays out each checklist item as a button with a checkbox and text, left aligned.
sections.why: Makes each item clickable.

sections.name: .checklist-group li button.selected
sections.title: Selected checklist item
sections.what: Gives the selected item a background.
sections.why: Shows which task is open.

sections.name: .check-box
sections.title: Checkbox box
sections.what: Draws a small bordered square for the checkbox.
sections.why: Shows the item's status.

sections.name: .check-box.done
sections.title: Done checkbox
sections.what: Fills the checkbox in green with a pop animation.
sections.why: Shows the item is complete.

sections.name: .check-box.active
sections.title: Active checkbox
sections.what: Colours the checkbox gold to mark the current item.
sections.why: Highlights the item in progress.

sections.name: .check-text
sections.title: Checklist item text block
sections.what: Lays out the item's title and details in a column.
sections.why: Keeps text stacked neatly.

sections.name: .check-text strong
sections.title: Checklist item title
sections.what: Styles the item title with truncation on one line.
sections.why: Keeps titles short in the list.

sections.name: .checklist-group.done .check-text strong
sections.title: Completed group title
sections.what: Dims the title of items in a completed group.
sections.why: Shows completed groups as secondary.

sections.name: .check-text small
sections.title: Checklist item details
sections.what: Styles the detail line with dim small text and truncation.
sections.why: Gives extra context without crowding.

sections.name: .check-text small i
sections.title: Detail colour dot
sections.what: Makes the small colour dot in a detail line round and fixed in size.
sections.why: Matches the dot to the detail text.

sections.name: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)
sections.title: Reduced motion for checklist
sections.what: Turns off the checkbox pop and progress transition for users who prefer reduced motion.
sections.why: Respects the user's motion setting.

sections.name: .lifecycle-strip
sections.title: Lifecycle strip layout
sections.what: Places the lifecycle summary and lanes side by side with a divider below.
sections.why: Shows the lifecycle view in one band.

sections.name: .lifecycle-now
sections.title: Current lifecycle status
sections.what: Stacks the current status in a centred column.
sections.why: Shows the current stage clearly.

sections.name: .lifecycle-now strong
sections.title: Current lifecycle heading
sections.what: Sets the current stage name to a smaller bold size.
sections.why: Makes the name prominent.

sections.name: .lifecycle-now small
sections.title: Current lifecycle note
sections.what: Styles the note below the current stage in small dim text.
sections.why: Adds context without distraction.

sections.name: .lifecycle-lanes
sections.title: Lifecycle lanes container
sections.what: Makes the lane area a relative grid for bars and the playhead.
sections.why: Lets bars and the playhead be placed inside.

sections.name: .lifecycle-lane
sections.title: Lifecycle lane row
sections.what: Lays out each lane as label, track and count columns with small dim text.
sections.why: Shows each lifecycle lane clearly.

sections.name: .lifecycle-lane.active
sections.title: Active lifecycle lane
sections.what: Makes the active lane's text bright.
sections.why: Shows which lane is current.

sections.name: .lifecycle-track
sections.title: Lifecycle track
sections.what: Draws the thin rounded background track for each lane.
sections.why: Gives bars a base to sit on.

sections.name: .lifecycle-bar
sections.title: Lifecycle bar
sections.what: Places a faded rounded bar across the track with a minimum visible width.
sections.why: Shows the span of work for a lane.

sections.name: .lifecycle-lane.active .lifecycle-bar
sections.title: Active lifecycle bar
sections.what: Makes the active lane's bar fully opaque with a glow.
sections.why: Draws attention to the current lane.

sections.name: .lifecycle-count
sections.title: Lifecycle count
sections.what: Aligns the count to the right with tabular numbers.
sections.why: Keeps numbers lined up.

sections.name: .lifecycle-playhead
sections.title: Playhead line
sections.what: Draws a thin vertical line over the lanes that ignores the mouse.
sections.why: Marks the current point in time.
sections.watch_out: Ignoring the mouse keeps it from blocking clicks on bars.

sections.name: @media (max-width: 760px)
sections.title: Lifecycle strip on small screens
sections.what: Stacks the lifecycle summary and lanes in one column on screens up to 760px.
sections.why: Fits the strip on narrow screens.

sections.name: .lifecycle-chip
sections.title: Lifecycle stage chip
sections.what: Styles stage chips as small outlined rounded labels.
sections.why: Shows each stage label compactly.

sections.name: .viewer-shell.workspace .scene-error
sections.title: Error card placement
sections.what: Places the scene error card above the floating tools, centred, with a shadow and a size limit.
sections.why: Keeps the error actions reachable when the 3D view is unavailable.
sections.watch_out: The top offset uses the timeline space, so the card moves when the timeline changes.

summary: Styles the full-screen 3D workspace: the floating tool panels, the bottom timeline, the top dock bar, the element list, the work checklist, the lifecycle strip and the error card.
purpose: Makes the 3D view fill the screen while tools float above it, and keeps the layout usable on narrow screens and for users who prefer reduced motion.
why: The workspace is a layout where the 3D view is the base and everything else sits on top. Separate rules keep the floating tools readable without blocking the view. Some rules are in media queries so narrow screens get a simpler layout.
how: The workspace rules set the main shell and reserve space at the bottom for the timeline by using a variable that grows when the timeline or lifecycle strip is shown. The stage and its badges and hints are placed over the 3D view. Floating panels get a border, background and shadow, with a grab handle header. Dock buttons sit in a rounded bar at the top. Checklist and layer list rules style rows, checkboxes and progress bars. Lifecycle rules draw timeline lanes and a playhead. Media queries change layout below 1100px and 760px widths. Motion is removed for users who ask for reduced motion.
inputs: Class names applied by the interface, such as viewer-shell workspace, floating-panel, workspace-dock, checklist-panel, lifecycle-strip and scene-error. Browser screen width and motion preference.
outputs: Visual layout only. No data is produced.
risks: Several widths are fixed in rem or calc values, so changing a number such as the timeline space can move panels onto each other. Some max-width values use calc with subtraction that may become negative on small screens, which browsers ignore. Some styles are repeated in other stylesheets, so a later rule can override these.
debug: If panels overlap or are cut off, check the timeline space variable and the width values in the media queries. If a button looks wrong, check the aria-pressed rules. If motion still plays for reduced motion users, check that the rule for that media query applies to the element.
